title: Ownership-aware memory allocation curves
question: How do declared neural, lexical, semantic, and hybrid target ownership allocations affect task-specific retention, dependence, and learning curves?
hypothesis: The allocation sweep can be nonmonotonic: neither all-neural nor zero-neural supervision is assumed to be optimal for every task or checkpoint.
failure_interpretation: A flat, U-shaped, or otherwise nonmonotonic curve is retained as observed evidence; it does not establish saved tokens, measured FLOPs, or a universal allocation policy.
controls: Bind every coordinate to a versioned allocation manifest with aligned owner/query arrays, source and tokenizer identity, verified semantic EngramPack identity, resource regime, and ownership profile.
Cross five ownership profiles and five neural-loss weights within each denominator design while fixing seed, packed source, runtime, optimizer, architecture, stopping policy, and task cards.
Keep raw input tokens, valid supervised targets, and weighted neural supervision mass as distinct counters.
Evaluate each declared card at every immutable observed checkpoint and retain each checkpoint identity without choosing a best point.
confounders: Ownership mixes, task dependency, and allocation-manifest contents change together; weight alone is not a compute measurement.
The five named resource regimes are denominator views over fixed architecture and token-budget runs, not independent replications or distinct model-size treatments.
Semantic results depend on the verified EngramPack and query provenance, not an unverified encoder.
Finite/repeated offline curricula and task-card wording limit generalization.
FLOPs use a rough 6 × active-parameters-per-token × measured-raw-tokens proxy; this is estimated accounting, while token and supervision counters are measured runtime counts.
hardware_notes: Run each denominator design with the same selected backend. Iso-FLOP uses a rough parameter-based estimate, not measured compute, speed, or energy.
runtime_class: Qualitative bounded educational workload; checkpoint curves may be nonmonotonic and no elapsed-time or FLOP result is implied.

endpoint_cards: all declared cards at every immutable observed checkpoint

papers.title: Engram
papers.claim_boundary: Motivates memory allocation questions; this recipe reports only SparseLab's manifest-bound observed points.

can_establish: Manifest-bound raw per-task, per-checkpoint allocation observations in each declared comparison regime.
Whether observed retention, dependence, or validation curves are nonmonotonic at the actually evaluated allocation points.
cannot_establish: Measured FLOP savings, latency, energy use, saved tokens, a smoothed optimum, or an allocation result transferred across a different task, pack, tokenizer, or source identity.
prerequisites: Each selected allocation-manifest path must be built and verified before training; it binds source/tokenizer/owner/query arrays and semantic EngramPack identity.
Semantic and hybrid ownership require verified semantic query artifacts rather than a guessed encoder.
